doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Norway ship jazz parties and Dizzy Gillespie
summary: On Hank O'Neil's Norway ship jazz parties he played with Dizzy Gillespie and Doc Cheatham; festival directors lack drawing cards.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah Hank O’Neil out of New York. And we were playing this session, they wanted a jam session so we had Dizzy Gillespie and I forget he was a reed player, the tall younger guy, great, great player, Doc Cheatham, you know, who was better than a lot of people gave him credit for. I tuned in Johnny Carson or somebody one night and he’s sitting in with the band. And Dizzy was great. And we were just — but it seemed like there were more black players left over from the big band era. And I had a festival — several festival directors in Europe say, “We have no drawing cards — the Dizzies and the —”
Milt Hintons, they’re all gone now.
But there are some around but it’s so difficult to get them interested. I think the schools that promote jazz I know I’ve done a couple of things with UCF —
